_comment: Placeholder content overlay. The real values live in content.local.json (git-ignored). acts lists the acts a generation can be launched as. Where the library is, where the apps' checkouts are, Genau's flick words, the inbox folder a Genau flick is dropped in and the folder the toolbar's audio switch plays from are not here: they are the settings all of Haglio shares, written once in ~/.haglio/settings.json (app_support.haglio_settings). pinned_kino_settings is optional as well: an act named here pins the gallery's Combine to this hand-tuned workflow+params (any param unnamed falls to the workflow's defaults, seeds are re-rolled per launch) instead of taking settings from past videos — the way out when an act's past videos all share a weakness. pinned_genau_settings is the same table for Combine's Genau lane, which makes one looping cycle rather than a full-length video: the key is the act again, so the two tables are separate — one keyed by act alone could hold an act's long-form settings or its loop's, never both. Both are optional, and an act missing from one is mined from past videos instead (for the Genau lane, only from videos a looping workflow made). detail_fix_parts is optional: extra parts the spoken "fix <part>" command can aim the enhance's detail pass at, beyond the built-in faces/hands/teeth/eyes — name is the word captions use, spoken the words the command may say, matches the filename substrings that recognize an installed detector (under ComfyUI's models/ultralytics/bbox) as finding it, and shared_photos false trains the part's LoRA on its own folder of photos alone, never on the fixes folder's shared one. search_synonyms is optional: extra groups of interchangeable words for the gallery search, each group a list of single words that all satisfy a query for any other — the built-in table in origenerator/search.py is general English, so vocabulary describing the library itself goes here. A group sharing a word with a built-in group extends it rather than replacing it; multi-word entries are ignored, since matching is word by word. speech_python is optional: the full path of the Python interpreter of the environment Qwen3-TTS is installed in (the app runs origenerator/speech_worker.py under it to speak a story's scene lines); omit it and a run with lines fails at submit saying no voice is set up. picture_states lists, in the order the sorting window lays them out, the mutually exclusive things a still image can be sorted as showing - what is already in frame when an animation starts from it; an image carries at most one, recorded on its row. animation_paths says which animations are worth asking for: per lane (video, the full-length clip, and genau, the single looping cycle), per act, the picture_states an animation of that act can sensibly start from. An act missing from a lane can be asked for from no image at all, and a state missing from an act's list answers a command naming it by saying so rather than animating something that cannot work. Every act named here must be one of acts, and every state one of picture_states. model_recommendations is what each checkpoint file's own page recommends, keyed by the file's name: the model's name as the page gives it, the samplers it names (each with the step spacings it pairs that sampler with, or none when it names none), steps and cfg as [lowest, highest], and the start a fresh form takes on that model; lora_recommendations is the same for a LoRA file, with strength, cfg, steps and shift. A setting outside what a page recommends wears a warning that quotes the page's name.

params.positive_prompt: gamma form, an example scene unfolds
beta form, one complete example motion, returning to where it began

genau_flick_prompts.positive: (one complete alpha cycle: all the way out, then all the way in, then return:1.5), (long travel:1.4)

beta.positive: (one complete beta cycle: all the way down, then all the way up, then return:1.5), (long travel:1.4)
